At a glance

Best months
April to June for breeding birds across the whole country, September and October for passage, November and February for cranes
Regions
The Camargue and the CrauProvence, the Calanques and the Hyeres salinsLanguedoc, the Aude lagoons and the eastern PyreneesThe Grands Causses and the GorgesThe PyreneesLac du Der and ChampagneThe Chatillonnais and the Forets national parkThe Baie de Somme and the Picardy coastBrittany, the Sept-Iles and OuessantThe Loire estuary, the Briere and Grand-LieuThe Vendee coast and the Marais PoitevinArcachon, Le Teich and the LandesThe Brenne and the SologneThe Alps: the Vanoise, the Ecrins and the MercantourAlsace, the Vosges and the RhineCorsica
Itineraries
A Camargue Week7 daysVultures and Mountains10 daysThe Crane Weekend3 daysThe Atlantic Coast8 daysCorsica End to End8 days
Getting around
A hire car is the honest answer almost everywhere on this page. The TGV reaches Arles, Strasbourg, Nantes and La Rochelle in under four hours from Paris, and Corsica needs a ferry or a flight

When to Go

France is sixteen regions in three climates, so the right month depends far more on where you go than on the year as a whole. The strip below is a national view; each region card says what its own season is.

Spring

March to June

Everything arrives at once. Herons and terns are back in the Camargue by late March, the Brenne fills with whiskered terns in May, and the Pyrenean and Alpine snowline retreats far enough to walk to by June.

Go for Full song, breeding plumage, and the widest choice of regions of any season.

Trade off The high passes in the Alps and the Pyrenees stay shut into June, so a mountain trip before then is a valley trip.

Typical daily average the Camargue 6 to 27 °C / 43 to 81 °F, Brittany 5 to 18 °C / 41 to 64 °F, Alsace 3 to 23 °C / 37 to 73 °F, the high Alps -9 to 8 °C / 16 to 46 °F

Summer and autumn

July to October

The mountains open properly in July and August, and from late August the Atlantic coast and the western Pyrenean passes carry the southbound migration.

Go for Alpine and Pyrenean ground at its most reachable, then raptor and crane passage over the Basque passes and waders on the Atlantic bays.

Trade off July and August are the French holiday months, so the coast is busy and rooms cost the most.

Typical daily average the Camargue 11 to 30 °C / 52 to 86 °F, Brittany 10 to 20 °C / 50 to 68 °F, Alsace 7 to 26 °C / 45 to 79 °F, the high Alps -1 to 13 °C / 30 to 55 °F

Winter

November to February

Cranes fill Champagne, the Camargue holds its flamingos and raptors through the cold, and the Atlantic bays carry their biggest wader counts of the year.

Go for The crane roost at Lac du Der, the cheapest rooms of the year, and a Camargue with nobody on it.

Trade off Eight or nine hours of daylight, and the mountain regions are effectively closed to birding.

Typical daily average the Camargue 3 to 14 °C / 37 to 57 °F, Brittany 5 to 12 °C / 41 to 54 °F, Alsace 0 to 8 °C / 32 to 46 °F, the high Alps -10 to -1 °C / 14 to 30 °F

A Camargue Week

The shape almost every operator sells, and the one to copy if you self-drive. One base in or near Arles reaches the lagoons, the salt pans and the steppe without moving hotel.

Vultures and Mountains

Toulouse (TLS), the Grands Causses, the Pyrenees, Toulouse

Four vulture species over the causses, then the high Pyrenean valleys for Lammergeier, Wallcreeper and the alpine list. June to September, once the passes are open.

The Crane Weekend

Paris Charles de Gaulle (CDG), Lac du Der, Paris

Two hours from Paris and built around two dawns at the roost. November and February are the peaks. This is a self-drive trip rather than an operator product.

The Atlantic Coast

Nantes (NTE), the Loire estuary, the Marais Poitevin, Arcachon, Bordeaux

A run down the west coast taking in three of the best wader sites in France and finishing at Le Teich. Best on autumn passage or in mid winter, when the counts are highest.

Corsica End to End

Bastia (BIA), the eastern lagoons, Corte, the Vergio pass, Ajaccio

The island's two endemics live in the high pine forest and the lagoons on the east coast add flamingo and Audouin's Gull, so the trip runs coast to mountain and back.

The Camargue and the Crau

Lagoon, salt pan and stony steppe in the Rhone delta, an hour from Marseille

The delta where the Rhone reaches the Mediterranean is the single most productive place to bird in France, and the one every operator on this page routes through. Brackish lagoons, salt pans and reed hold flamingos, herons and terns, and the dry Crau steppe just east of it holds a different list again on the same day.

Look for: Greater Flamingo, Slender-billed Gull, Little Bustard, Pin-tailed Sandgrouse, Squacco Heron, Collared Pratincole

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional de Camargue (regional park), Reserve naturelle nationale de Camargue (national nature reserve), Reserve naturelle nationale des Coussouls de Crau (national nature reserve)

Stops: , a private reserve with made paths and hides through lagoon and reed, and the surest close view of flamingos in France. Open daily, entry charged , the great central lagoon of the delta, watched from the road along its eastern shore rather than entered. The core of the national nature reserve , the reserve's own information centre on the east shore of the Vaccarès, with a short trail and hides over freshwater marsh , former salt workings inside the national nature reserve, permit only from La Capelière, with hides over shallow pools , the sea wall between the lagoons and the beach, walked or cycled, with the salt pans on one side and the sea on the other , reed, wet grazing and open water east of the delta, with marked trails and a tower. Bitterns and harriers , the stony steppe east of the delta, the last of its kind in western Europe, grazed by sheep. This is the ground for Little Bustard, sandgrouse and Lesser Kestrel , the salt-pan lagoon where France's flamingos breed, on an island built for them, watched from the dike at a distance that keeps the colony settled

Visitor centres: La Capeliere information centre, Musee de la Camargue, Arles

Also covers: Arles, Aubais, Aubussargues, Baillargues, Carnon Plage, Domaine et Golf de Pont Royal, estézargues, Fontvieille, Istres, La Grande-Motte, Lagnes, Lattes, Lauris, Le Grau-du-Roi, Les Baux de Provence, Les Baux-de-Provence, Lunel, Mallemort, Marguerittes, MARTIGUES, Mauguio, Miramas, PALAVAS-LES-FLOTS, Paradou, Remoulins, Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, Salon-de-Provence, Sommières

Also watch for: Camargue horses and black bulls are worked on the delta and are part of what keeps the marsh open. Beavers are back on the Rhone arms, and the salt pans carry huge numbers of dragonflies from May.

Where to Stay78 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. Provence, the Calanques and the Hyeres salins

White limestone sea cliffs and worked salt pans between Marseille and the Iles d'Hyeres

Two national parks sit within an hour of each other on this coast and they do entirely different work. The Calanques are limestone inlets and offshore islands where Bonelli's Eagle nests within sight of Marseille and the Riou archipelago carries the shearwater and storm petrel colonies. Ninety minutes east, the old salt pans at Hyeres are a Ramsar wetland of pans, dunes and a tombolo, and Port-Cros protects the islands beyond them. The Camargue is the bigger name on this coast, and this is the stretch of it that holds the breeding seabirds.

Look for: Bonelli's Eagle, Scopoli's Shearwater, European Storm Petrel, Eurasian Eagle-Owl, Blue Rock Thrush, Greater Flamingo, Pied Avocet, Audouin's Gull

Parks and reserves: Parc national des Calanques, Parc national de Port-Cros, Reserve naturelle nationale de la Plaine des Maures (national nature reserve)

Stops: , a worked salt pan on the Giens tombolo, walked on the tracks around its edge. Around 350 species are recorded across the Hyeres salins on 900 hectares, and flamingos are on the water all year , the older and larger of the two Hyeres salt pans, east of the town, with a free marked path and screens. Stilts and avocets from March , the double sand bar running out to the Giens headland, with the salt pan between its two arms and a sea watch off the point , the wooded island at the heart of the national park, reached by ferry from Hyeres or Le Lavandou, with marked paths and no cars. France's first marine national park , the largest of the Iles d'Hyeres, part of the same national park, with salt pans, pine and cliff on the south shore. Ferries from La Tour Fondue , the seabird islands south of Marseille, inside the Calanques national park and closed to landing in the breeding season. Watched from a boat or from the cliffs above Callelongue , reached on foot from the Luminy campus gate, the usual way into the park on the Marseille side. Summer access is by permit and the number is capped , the highest sea cliff in France, driven along the Route des Cretes above Cassis, with Alpine Swift and Blue Rock Thrush on the face and a sea watch below , the four islands off the Vieux-Port, in the national park, reached by the year-round passenger boat. Scopoli's Shearwater breeds here and on Riou

Visitor centres: Maison du Parc national de Port-Cros, Hyeres, Maison du Parc national des Calanques, Marseille

Also covers: Bandol, Bormes-les-Mimosas, Cabriès, CAP ESTEREL, Carcès, CARRY LE ROUET, Carry-le-Rouet, Châteauneuf-le-Rouge, Cogolin, Domaine du Thronnet, Fuveau, Gémenos, Grimaud, ILE ROUSSE, La Farlède, La Seyne-sur-Mer, La Valette-du-Var, Le Grand Boisset, LE LAVANDOU, Marignane, Sainte-Maxime, SAUSSET LES PINS, SIX FOURS LES PLAGES, Six-Fours-Les-Plages, St. Tropez, Toulon

Also watch for: Yelkouan Shearwater breeds on the Riou islands and has no card in the guide yet, so it is named here in prose rather than linked. Bottlenose dolphins and striped dolphins work the water off the Calanques, and the Port-Cros seagrass meadows are the reason the marine reserve exists.

Where to Stay130 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. Languedoc, the Aude lagoons and the eastern Pyrenees

Coastal lagoon, garrigue and the Mediterranean end of the Pyrenees, an hour from Perpignan

Where the Pyrenees run into the Mediterranean, a chain of coastal lagoons carries flamingos, gulls and terns within sight of mountains that hold Wallcreeper. Two operators sell this ground as its own week, and it answers a different question from the high Pyrenees three hundred kilometres west.

Look for: Greater Flamingo, Audouin's Gull, Purple Swamphen, Slender-billed Gull, Moustached Warbler, European Bee-eater

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional de la Narbonnaise en Mediterranee (regional park), Parc naturel regional des Pyrenees catalanes (regional park)

Stops: , a shallow coastal lagoon south of Perpignan with a reserve, a path and reed beds. Flamingos, terns and Moustached Warbler , a large brackish lagoon behind the coast, watched from the road and the tracks between the oyster beds , the biggest of the Aude lagoons, inside the regional park, with viewpoints at Bages and Peyriac-de-Mer , a dry limestone massif between Narbonne and the sea, with Bonelli's Eagle country and warblers in the garrigue , a narrow gorge in the Corbières below the Cathar castles, with Alpine Swift, Crag Martin and raptors overhead , the eastern Pyrenean reserve above the Tech valley, forest to alpine, and the closest high ground to the coast , the mountain that stands over Roussillon, reached by track from Vernet-les-Bains, with the eastern Pyrenean list

Visitor centres: Maison du Parc, Sigean

Also covers: Agde, Aigues-Vives, Argelès-sur-Mer, Banyuls-sur-Mer, Beziers, Boujan-sur-Libron, Cami del Segre, Canet-en-Roussillon, Côte Ouest, Couiza, MOSSET, Moulin de Graïs, Narbonne, Opoul-Périllos, Place Sant Genis, Port-Vendres, Promenade de l'ancien stade, Rivesaltes, Saissac, Saleilles, serignan, VERDUN EN LAURAGAIS, Vias, Villepinte

Also watch for: The Corbières garrigue carries Hermann's tortoise and Montpellier snake, and the lagoons are among the best French ground for dragonflies.

Where to Stay74 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. The Grands Causses and the Gorges

Limestone plateau and gorge in the southern Massif Central, two hours from Montpellier

Four species of vulture fly over one set of gorges here, which is true almost nowhere else in Europe. Griffons were brought back to the Gorges de la Jonte in the early 1980s and Cinereous followed a decade later, and the plateau between the gorges is open sheep country with its own list.

Look for: Griffon Vulture, Cinereous Vulture, Egyptian Vulture, Bearded Vulture, Short-toed Snake Eagle, Ortolan Bunting

Parks and reserves: Parc national des Cevennes, Parc naturel regional des Grands Causses (regional park)

Stops: , the vulture centre above the Gorges de la Jonte, with a viewpoint straight into the colony and a live nest camera. This is the single best vulture watchpoint in France , the road along the gorge floor between Le Rozier and Meyrueis, with pull-ins under the cliffs the vultures use , the deeper gorge to the north, the same birds with more traffic, and Crag Martin and Alpine Swift over the villages , the high plateau between the two gorges, open sheep-grazed limestone. Ortolan Bunting, Tawny Pipit and Short-toed Lark on the tracks , the plateau south of the Jonte, quieter than the Mejean and reached from Le Rozier , a meander cut deep into the causse south of Millau, with raptors along the rim

Visitor centres: Maison des Vautours, Le Truel

Also covers: Avène, Berrias-et-Casteljau, Brissac, Domaine d'Anglas, Gages, Le Vigan, MENDE, Moulin d'Angles, Saint-Affrique, Salvinsac, ST SERNIN SUR RANCE

Also watch for: Przewalski's horses are kept on the Causse Mejean, and the plateau carries orchids through May and June.

The Pyrenees

High mountain, cirque and forest along the Spanish border, two hours from Pau or Toulouse

The French side of the range is where a first Lammergeier is realistic, and the walk to a cirque puts Wallcreeper, Alpine Accentor and Citril Finch on the same morning. Two national park valleys, Ossau in the west and Gavarnie in the centre, carry most of the operator itineraries.

Look for: Bearded Vulture, Wallcreeper, Alpine Accentor, Citril Finch, White-winged Snowfinch, Rock Ptarmigan

National park: Parc national des Pyrenees

Stops: , the great amphitheatre at the head of the valley, walked from the village in about an hour and a half. Wallcreeper on the walls and vultures over the rim , a paid car park above Cauterets, and the start of the walk to the Lac de Gaube. Forest below, alpine above, Citril Finch on the treeline , the pass at the head of the Ossau valley on the Spanish border, high open ground reached by road , a high road pass between the Ossau and Azun valleys, with alpine meadow and cliff either side , a griffon colony in the Ossau valley with a visitor centre and cameras into the nests , the western national park valley, forest to alpine within an hour's drive, and the classic route for Lammergeier , a Basque country pass on the western edge, one of the great autumn raptor and crane watchpoints in Europe, staffed from July to November

Visitor centres: Falaise aux Vautours visitor centre, Aste-Beon

Also covers: ARUDY, Ax les Thermes, Bruges, La Bastide-de-Sérou, Loudenvielle, Lourdes, MONTGAILLARD, Oloron Sainte-Marie, Saint-Lary-Soulan, Sazos

Also watch for: Izard, the Pyrenean chamois, is common in the national park, and marmots whistle from the scree above every valley head.

Lac du Der and Champagne

A very large reservoir in flat farmland, two hours east of Paris

The crane migration through Champagne is the biggest wildlife spectacle in northern France, and Lac du Der is where it stops. Birds roost on the drawn-down reservoir and fly out to the stubbles at dawn, and the same water holds White-tailed Eagle and thousands of duck through the winter.

Look for: Common Crane, White-tailed Eagle, Greylag Goose, Great Egret, Osprey, Black Woodpecker

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional de la Foret d'Orient (regional park), Reserve naturelle nationale de l'Etang de la Horre (national nature reserve)

Stops: , the reservoir itself, watched from a ring of signed viewpoints. Water is drawn down through autumn, which is what creates the roost , a crane observation site in the fields west of the lake, staffed in season, where the birds feed after leaving the roost , a peninsula viewpoint on the south shore, one of the standard dawn fly-out watchpoints , a shallow national nature reserve pool south of the lake, quieter, with reed and marsh birds , one of the Aube forest lakes south of the Der, in the regional park, with the same birds and far fewer people

Visitor centres: Maison du Lac du Der, Sainte-Marie-du-Lac-Nuisement

Also covers: GIFFAUMONT CHAMPAUBERT, MESNIL ST PERE, Saint-Dizier, Troyes

Also watch for: The oak forest around the lake is old and wet, and beavers work the feeder streams.

The Chatillonnais and the Forets national park

Beech and oak plateau on the Champagne and Burgundy border, three hours south-east of Paris

France's eleventh national park was declared in 2019 and is the first anywhere in the country for lowland broadleaf forest rather than mountain or coast. Three massifs of beech and oak run across the Champagne and Burgundy border on limestone plateau, cut by narrow valleys and dotted with about a hundred tufa marshes. Six pairs of Black Stork breed here, against seventy to ninety in the whole of France, and the park carries the largest integral forest reserve in metropolitan France at 3,087 hectares.

Look for: Black Stork, Middle Spotted Woodpecker, Grey-headed Woodpecker, Black Woodpecker, Red Kite, European Honey Buzzard

National park: Parc national de forets

Stops: , the Haute-Marne massif, worked from the village of Arc-en-Barrois that it surrounds and that the park is run from. Three woodpecker species breed in the old stands. OpenStreetMap carries no boundary for the forest itself, so the coordinate here is the village , a twelfth century abbey deep inside the Chatillon massif at Villiers-le-Duc, open to visitors, and the readiest way into the Cote-d'Or half of the park. Forest on every side of it , 3,087 hectares left entirely to themselves since December 2021, the largest of its kind in metropolitan France. A research reserve rather than a visit, and access is regulated , the park's interpretation centre on the Burgundy side, with the forest ecology displays and the walk information for the Chatillon massif , a Cistercian abbey in the Aube valley at the south-east corner of the park, and the village the Black Stork ringing work is run from , a resurgence spring rising at the foot of a cliff in the middle of Chatillon-sur-Seine, and the easiest introduction to the limestone hydrology the whole park sits on , a walled medieval deer park on the edge of the village, open and free, with fallow deer inside and the forest edge birds along its wall

Visitor centres: Maison du Parc national de forets, Chateauvillain, Maison de la Foret, Leuglay

Also covers: AUBERIVE, Chaumont, Fresnes, Langres, Monaco, Sarcey, VANVEY, Villegusien-le-Lac

Also watch for: Red deer, roe deer and wild boar are the reason much of this forest was kept, and the rut at Chateauvillain is the set piece of the autumn. European wildcat holds across the massifs. The park has some of the darkest skies in France, which is worth an evening for owls and nightjar as much as for stars.

The Baie de Somme and the Picardy coast

Tidal bay, dune and saltmarsh, two hours north of Paris

The Somme estuary is the largest tidal bay on the French Channel coast and the closest serious wader ground to Paris. The Marquenterre reserve behind the dunes gives made paths and hides, and the bay itself fills and empties on a big tide that pushes birds within reach.

Look for: Pied Avocet, Eurasian Spoonbill, Bar-tailed Godwit, Kentish Plover, Common Shelduck, Bluethroat

Parks and reserves: Reserve naturelle nationale de la Baie de Somme (national nature reserve), Parc naturel marin des estuaires picards et de la mer d'Opale (marine park)

Stops: , a reserve of lagoon, dune and pine behind the bay, with three marked circuits and staffed hides. Spoonbill and heron colonies , the estuary itself, watched from the sea walls at Le Crotoy and Saint-Valery on a rising tide , the national nature reserve covering the northern bay, of which the Marquenterre is the visitable part , shingle, pools and rough grazing at the southern end of the bay, free to walk and good for passage , a low headland at Saint-Valery with a view across the channel of the bay

Visitor centres: Maison de la Baie de Somme, Lanchères

Also covers: Abbeville, Ault, Flers, Fleury, Fort-Mahon-Plage, Merlimont, Montreuil, Promenade du Marquenterre, Ramburelles, SAINT OUEN, Saint-Ouen

Also watch for: Harbour and grey seals haul out on the sandbanks in the middle of the bay and are visible from the shore at low water.

Brittany, the Sept-Iles and Ouessant

Seabird island, granite headland and estuary, four hours west of Paris by train

France's seabirds are concentrated on a handful of Breton islands, and the Sept-Iles holds the country's only gannet colony along with puffins and auks. Out at the western tip, Ouessant is the French rarity island, and its autumn does what Fair Isle does for Britain.

Look for: Northern Gannet, Atlantic Puffin, Razorbill, Common Murre, European Storm Petrel, Red-billed Chough

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel marin d'Iroise (marine park), Parc naturel regional d'Armorique (regional park), Reserve naturelle nationale des Sept-Iles (national nature reserve)

Stops: , the seabird islands off Perros-Guirec, worked by boat from the harbour. Landing is only on Ile aux Moines; the gannets and auks are watched from the water , the westernmost French island, reached by ferry from Le Conquet or Brest. Autumn brings seabird passage off the headlands and rarities in the gardens , an LPO cliff reserve west of Douarnenez with a marked path along the seabird ledges, best from April to July , the classic Breton headland at the end of the Cap Sizun, and a seawatch point in an onshore blow , a high headland on the Crozon peninsula, another seawatch station, with Chough on the cliff grass , a shingle bar with lagoons behind it along the south side of the Cap Sizun, good for waders and passage

Visitor centres: Station LPO de l'Ile-Grande

Also covers: Brest, CAMARET SUR MER, Carantec, Corniche de la Mer, Crozon, DOUARNENEZ, Guipavas, Hent Kerveltrec, KERIDREUFF TY VARLEN, Landerneau, Lannion, Le Guilvinec, PERROS GUIREC, PLEUMEUR BODOU, PLOUBAZLANEC, PLOUEZEC, Plouider, Ploumagoar, POULDREUZIC, SANTEC

Also watch for: Grey seals breed on the Sept-Iles and in the Iroise, and the Iroise sea is one of the few French waters with resident bottlenose dolphins.

The Loire estuary, the Briere and Grand-Lieu

Marsh, reed and shallow lake around Nantes, two hours from Paris by train

Three different wetlands sit within an hour of Nantes: the salt pans at Guerande, the reed and open water of the Briere, and Lac de Grand-Lieu, which is the largest natural lowland lake in France in winter and holds a heron colony that is nationally important.

Look for: Purple Heron, Eurasian Spoonbill, Whiskered Tern, Bluethroat, Black-winged Stilt, Eurasian Bittern

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional de Briere (regional park), Reserve naturelle nationale du Lac de Grand-Lieu (national nature reserve)

Stops: , a shallow lake south-west of Nantes whose core is closed, watched from the observatory at Passay and the LPO site at Saint-Philbert , the interpretation centre on the north shore with a tower over the reed , the marsh north of Saint-Nazaire, worked from the canal paths and the causeways at Saint-Lyphard and Saint-Andre-des-Eaux , working salt pans between Guerande and Le Croisic, watched from the tracks between the basins. Waders, terns and Bluethroat in the samphire , a seawatch point on the north side of the estuary mouth

Visitor centres: Maison du Lac de Grand-Lieu, Bouaye

Also covers: Clisson, CORSEPT, Couëron, Crossac, DOMAINE DE PELVEZY, Gétigné, Guérande, Ile-aux-moines, L'Aiguillon-sur-Vie, La Baule-Escoublac, LA CHAPELLE HERMIER, LA CHAPELLE SUR ERDRE, la roche sur yon, LE PLESSIS GRIMAUD, Le Pouliguen, Les Sables D'Olonne, Les Sables-d'Olonne, MISSILLAC, MUZILLAC, penvins, PIRIAC SUR MER, Port-Saint-Père, Rezé, SAINT BREVIN LES PINS, Saint-Brevin-les-Pins, Saint-Herblain, Saint-Nazaire, Treillières, Trignac

Also watch for: Coypu are everywhere in the Briere canals, and the salt pans at Guerande are still worked by hand.

Where to Stay112 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. The Vendee coast and the Marais Poitevin

Mudflat, wet meadow and canal marsh on the Atlantic coast, south of Nantes

The Baie de l'Aiguillon is one of the two or three most important wader sites in France, and the wet meadows and canals of the Marais Poitevin behind it hold a breeding list that has largely gone from the rest of lowland Europe. La Rochelle is the base, and everything is within an hour.

Look for: Black-tailed Godwit, Pied Avocet, Whiskered Tern, Bluethroat, Little Bustard, Eurasian Curlew

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional du Marais poitevin (regional park), Reserve naturelle nationale de la baie de l'Aiguillon (national nature reserve)

Stops: , the mudflats at the head of the Anse de l'Aiguillon, watched from the sea wall at Esnandes and the pointe de l'Aiguillon on a rising tide , a wet-meadow reserve with a staffed observatory, one of the best places in France to see breeding waders at close range , the canal marsh inland of the bay, worked from the paths around Coulon and Arcais , former salt pans at the northern tip of the Ile de Re, an LPO reserve with a path and hides , saltmarsh and lagoon south of Rochefort, an LPO reserve with a long trail and hides over the flats , a sand spit at the mouth of the Lay, a national nature reserve watched from its landward edge , a small reserve on Noirmoutier at the estuary's southern edge, with a colony of terns and gulls

Visitor centres: Maison du Marais poitevin, Coulon

Also covers: AUBIGNY LES CLOUZEAUX, av de Lattre de Tassigny, CHATELAILLON PLAGE, CHIZE, COULON, DAMVIX, Dolus-d'Oléron, Foussais-Payré, La Couarde-sur-Mer, LA FERRIERE, La Josephtrie, LE CHAY, Le Colombier, Le Fort de la Rade, Les Boucholeurs, Les Mathes, Mouilleron-le-Captif, Niort, NOIRMOUTIER EN L'ILE, place Drouet d Erlon, Pornic, PREFAILLES, Puilboreau, Royan, SAINT JULIEN DES LANDES, Saint-Just-Luzac, Saint-Trojan-les-Bains, SAINTE MARIE DE RE, Sainte Mégrine, Sainte-Marie-de-Ré, Saintes, Sèvres, Soulac-sur-Mer, ST CLEMENT DES BALEINES, Talmont-Saint-Hilaire, Tonnay-Charente, Virson

Also watch for: Otters use the Marais Poitevin canals, and the wet meadows carry Fritillary in April.

Where to Stay99 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. Arcachon, Le Teich and the Landes

Tidal basin, lagoon reserve and pine forest, an hour from Bordeaux

The Bassin d'Arcachon is a tidal basin with a wader reserve built into the delta of the Leyre, and the Parc ornithologique du Teich is the easiest place in south-west France to see spoonbills and waders from a hide. Behind it, the Landes pine forest runs south for a hundred kilometres.

Look for: Eurasian Spoonbill, Pied Avocet, Osprey, Bluethroat, Dartford Warbler, European Nightjar

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional des Landes de Gascogne (regional park), Reserve naturelle nationale du banc d'Arguin (national nature reserve)

Stops: , a reserve of lagoons and reed in the Leyre delta, with a long circuit and twenty hides. Open daily, entry charged, and the anchor of the region , a shifting sandbank at the mouth of the basin holding a Sandwich Tern colony, reached by boat from Arcachon and viewed from the Dune du Pilat , former fish ponds on the east side of the basin, with paths along the dikes and far fewer visitors than Le Teich , the wooded channels above the reserve, walked on marked paths from Le Teich , the great dune south of Arcachon, which gives the overview of the banc d'Arguin and the basin mouth

Visitor centres: Parc ornithologique du Teich

Also covers: ares, Bègles, Biganos, Biscarrosse, Castets, Eysines, LA TESTE DE BUCH, La Teste-de-Buch, Latresne, LE HAILLAN, MIMIZAN, Pessac, Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, VILLENAVE D'ORNON, Villenave-d'Ornon

Also watch for: The Dune du Pilat, the tallest sand dune in Europe, sits at the mouth of the basin and is worth an hour for the view over the banc d'Arguin.

Where to Stay87 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. The Brenne and the Sologne

Thousands of shallow fish ponds in central France, two hours south of Paris

The Brenne is a landscape of man-made fish ponds, more than two thousand of them, and it holds a breeding list that includes Whiskered Tern, Purple Heron and Black-necked Grebe in numbers that matter nationally. The Sologne to the north is the same idea under oak and heath, and quieter.

Look for: Whiskered Tern, Purple Heron, Black-necked Grebe, Eurasian Bittern, Savi's Warbler, European Honey Buzzard

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional de la Brenne (regional park), Reserve naturelle nationale de Cherine (national nature reserve)

Stops: , the core reserve of the Brenne, with four hides on marked paths and a nature house. Free to enter , one of the Cherine reserve's ponds, with the hide that gives the closest whiskered tern watching in France , the largest pond in the Brenne, viewed from its causeway , a large Sologne pond in oak and heath country, with a road along one side

Visitor centres: Maison du Parc, Rosnay

Also covers: Brigueil-le-Chantre, Candé-sur-Beuvron, Chaumont-sur-Tharonne, Chémery, EGUZON CHANTOME, Ingrandes, LATHUS ST REMY, Lavoux, Le Poinçonnet, Les Saules, Maslives, Monthou-sur-Cher, Ouchamps, Poilly-lez-Gien, Poulaines, Saint-Denis-sur-Loire, SELLES ST DENIS, ST DENIS SUR LOIRE, Tours

Also watch for: European Pond Terrapin is native here and basks on the pond margins from April, which is unusual enough in France to be worth looking for.

The Alps: the Vanoise, the Ecrins and the Mercantour

High alpine meadow, larch forest and rock, two hours from Grenoble or Nice

Three national parks hold the French alpine list, and a cable car or a high road pass puts you into it without a mountaineering day. Bearded Vulture was reintroduced to the Alps from the 1980s and is now seen regularly in all three, and the Mercantour above Nice adds Mediterranean species to the alpine ones.

Look for: Bearded Vulture, Rock Ptarmigan, Black Grouse, White-winged Snowfinch, Alpine Accentor, Wallcreeper

National parks: Parc national de la Vanoise, Parc national des Ecrins, Parc national du Mercantour

Stops: , the highest paved pass in the Alps, above Bonneval-sur-Arc in the Vanoise, with snowfinch and accentor around the car park , a road-end viewpoint high in the Vanoise above Termignon, looking across the Doron to the glaciers. Ibex on the slopes and alpine birds around the car park , a pass between the Ecrins and the Briançonnais with an alpine botanic garden and easy high ground either side , the Mercantour valley above Nice, with the Alpha wolf park at Saint-Martin and forest to alpine within half an hour , a high Mercantour valley of rock and lake, a full day on foot, with ptarmigan and accentor on the tops , a walk up from Bourg-d'Arud into the Ecrins, through forest to a lake under the crags

Visitor centres: Maison du Parc national de la Vanoise, Pralognan

Also covers: Aime, Ancienne route de Baratier, AUTRANS, AV DE LA GRANDE MOTTE LE VAL CLARET, Beausoleil, Bourg-Saint-Maurice, BRIANCON, Chamrousse, Courchevel, Crots, Echirolles, Fontanil-Cornillon, Hameau Les Champs, LANSLEBOURG MONT CENIS, LE PLEYNET, Les Allues, Les Deux Alpes, Menton, Méribel Mottaret, Montbonnot-Saint-Martin, Montgenèvre, Pierre et Vacances la daille, Place Marcel Dumas Le Collet d'Allevard, Pont de labrau, Port de Cap d'Ail, Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, Saint Dalmas le Selvage, Saint Laurent du Var, Saint-Bon-Tarentaise, SAINT-CHAFFREY, Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat, Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne, Saint-Laurent-du-Var, Saint-Martin-de-Belleville, Sassenage, Seyssins, St Martin d'Uriage, Tende, Tignes, VACANCEOLE LE HAMEAU DE VALLOIRE CHEMIN DE LA CURIA, Val Thorens, Val-d'Isère, Valmorel, Vence, Villefranche-sur-Mer, Voreppe, ZAC Les Alpages de Chantel

Also watch for: Ibex were saved in the Vanoise and are now easy there, and wolves recolonised France through the Mercantour in 1992.

Alsace, the Vosges and the Rhine

Riverine forest, sandstone ridge and mountain, north-east on the German border

The Rhine floodplain forest, the Ried wet meadows and the Vosges ridge sit within an hour of Strasbourg, and between them they carry the French woodpecker list almost complete. White Stork was down to a handful of Alsatian pairs in the 1970s and is now on village roofs across the plain.

Look for: White Stork, Middle Spotted Woodpecker, Black Woodpecker, Grey-headed Woodpecker, Hazel Grouse, Red Kite

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional des Vosges du Nord (regional park), Parc naturel regional des Ballons des Vosges (regional park)

Stops: , Rhine floodplain forest on an island in the river inside the Strasbourg city limits, with marked paths , riverine forest and backwater where the Sauer meets the Rhine in the far north of Alsace , wet meadow along the Ill south of Sélestat, a landscape that has largely gone elsewhere on the plain , the sandstone and beech country in the north, a UNESCO biosphere reserve with the French woodpecker list , a high point on the main Vosges ridge above Munster, reached by road, with the alpine-edge species of the range , old Rhine channels and reed at the Swiss corner, with a ringing station and marked trails

Visitor centres: Maison du Parc des Vosges du Nord, La Petite-Pierre

Also covers: ARRENTES DE CORCIEUX, Baldersheim, Ban-sur-Meurthe-Clefcy, Barr, Bas-Rhin, BUHL LORRAINE, Bussang, Colroy-la-Roche, Dorlisheim, Eguisheim, F- NEUWILLER-LES-SAVERNE, Fouday, Geispolsheim, Gérardmer, Girmont-Val-d'Ajol, Hattigny, HORBOURG-WIHR, Illkirch-Graffenstaden, JONCHEREY, Kaysersberg-Vignoble, La Bresse, La Petite-Pierre, LALAYE, Le Bonhomme, Lucelle, Molsheim, Mutzig, NOMPATELIZE, Obernai, Ostwald, Remiremont, Riquewihr, SAINT PIERRE, Saint-Louis, Saint-Maurice, SAINT-PIERRE, Sarrebourg, Sausheim, Schiltigheim, Sélestat, ST PIERRE, STE MARIE AUX MINES, Vogelgrun, Wattwiller, Wolxheim

Also watch for: Lynx and, more recently, wolf are back in the Vosges, and the sandstone ridge in the north carries chamois that were introduced in the 1950s.

Where to Stay126 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. Corsica

Mountain, maquis and coastal lagoon, a ferry or a short flight from the mainland

Corsica is where the French list picks up birds that are on it nowhere else. The Corsican Nuthatch lives only in the island's laricio pine forest, the Corsican Finch is shared with Sardinia alone, and the coastal lagoons on the east side add flamingo and Audouin's Gull to a mountain trip.

Look for: Corsican Nuthatch, Corsican Finch, Marmora's Warbler, Audouin's Gull, Red Kite, Moltoni's Warbler

Parks and reserves: Parc naturel regional de Corse (regional park), Reserve naturelle des Bouches de Bonifacio (national nature reserve), Reserve naturelle de l'etang de Biguglia (national nature reserve)

Stops: , laricio pine forest above Evisa, the classic and most reliable site for Corsican Nuthatch, worked from the forest road , the highest road pass on the island, between the Aitone and Valdo-Niello forests, with nuthatch, Citril Finch and alpine ground above , the other great pine forest, on the Calacuccia side of the Vergio pass , the largest Corsican lagoon, just south of Bastia, a nature reserve with flamingos, waders and Moustached Warbler in the reed , a quieter east-coast lagoon behind the beach, with Audouin's Gull offshore , the road up from Corte into the central massif, forest to high lake, with Red Kite over the valley and Alpine Chough on the tops , the white cliffs at the southern tip, with shearwater passage in the strait and Blue Rock Thrush on the rock

Visitor centres: Maison du Parc naturel regional de Corse, Corte

Also covers: AGHIONE, Agosta plage, Albitreccia, ALERIA, Asco, BELVEDERE CAMPOMORO, BIGUGLIA, CALACUCCIA, CERVIONE, Chiatra, GHISONACCIA, L'ILE ROUSSE, ld Giustiniana BRAVONE, LECCI, moltifao, Plage d'Aregno, Poggio-Mezzana, Porto, PROPRIANO, QUENZA, SAGONE, SAN NICOLAO, Santo Pietro di Tenda, SERRA DI FERRO, Serra-di-Ferro

Also watch for: The mouflon is native here and lives in the high central massif, and the island has its own subspecies of red deer, brought back from Sardinian stock after it went extinct in the 1960s.

Where to Stay58 places to stay

Every place to stay on this page holds a current Green Key award, taken from the scheme's own register rather than from a property's own claim, and each chip links to the register row that proves it. What the register publishes is a name, a category, an address and a coordinate, so that is what these cards carry: there is no description here, because a certification says a property was audited against a checklist and says nothing about what staying there is like or how it treats the birds around it. Birding Community

Five organisations worth knowing before a French trip. Between them they manage most of the reserves named on this page and publish the counts behind it. Find a birding organisation near you in our worldwide directory

Alongside the national bodies below, France has 29 local bird clubs across 13 regions. They run the walks and the counts, and most of them welcome visitors. See every French club by region.

LPO BirdLife in France, and the manager of many of the reserves on this page including the Sept-Iles and Moeze-Oleron. Visit Bretagne Vivante The Breton nature society, which runs the Cap Sizun reserve and much of the seabird monitoring. Visit Tour du Valat The Camargue research institute, and the source behind most published flamingo and wetland figures. Visit Reserves naturelles de France The network body for the national nature reserves, with a searchable list of every one. Visit Faune-France The national participatory recording portal, run by LPO and the regional associations. Visit

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the best time to go birding in France?

April to June if you want one trip to cover the country, because that is when the lowland regions are in full song and the mountains are opening. September and October for passage on the Atlantic coast and over the western Pyrenean passes. November and February for the crane roost at Lac du Der.

Where should I go for a first French birding trip?

The Camargue. It has the widest list in the shortest drive, it works in every month of the year, and it is the region every operator sells, so there is more written about it than anywhere else in France. Base yourself in or near Arles and you can reach the lagoons, the salt pans and the Crau steppe without changing hotel.

Do I need a car?

For most of the regions on this page, yes. The reserves sit outside the towns and rural bus services are thin. The exceptions are the Camargue, where Arles is on the TGV and there are guided day trips from it, and Alsace, where Strasbourg's trams and regional trains reach the Rhine forest. Corsica needs a car once you are off the boat.

Which French birds can I see nowhere else?

One: the Corsican Nuthatch, which needs the mature laricio pine of the Corsican mountains. The Corsican Finch is shared only with Sardinia. Everything else on the French list is shared with a neighbour, which is what makes France a country of regions rather than of endemics.

Where do I see all four European vultures in a day?

The Gorges de la Jonte in the Grands Causses. Griffon, Cinereous, Egyptian and Bearded Vulture all fly over the same gorge, which is true of very few places in Europe. The Belvedere des Vautours above the gorge is free to look from and has a live camera into a nest.

Is the Camargue worth it in winter?

Yes, and it is the cheapest and emptiest time to go. The flamingos stay, the raptor list is at its best, and the Crau holds wintering Little Bustard. What you lose is the breeding herons and terns, which arrive from March.

Can I see Lammergeier in France?

Yes, in two places. The Pyrenees carry the native population and are the more reliable of the two; the Alpine birds descend from releases that began in the 1980s and are seen regularly in the Vanoise, the Ecrins and the Mercantour. Both are watched from valley heads and road passes.

What about France's overseas departements?

They each deserve a page of their own, and this one stays metropolitan. French Guiana, Reunion, Guadeloupe, Martinique and Mayotte hold avifaunas with their own families, their own seasons and their own endemics, and French Guiana in particular is a serious Neotropical destination that would be buried as a paragraph here.

How much does a French birding trip cost?

Accommodation is the largest line and France is a mid-priced European country for it. A guided operator week runs to several thousand dollars; the same ground self-driven costs a fraction of that, and most of the reserves on this page are free or charge a small entry.
